name: Men's Class A service dress coat, no shoulder boards: cadet NCO/airman, or base for the board overlay (nametag position only)
size_basis: Traced from images/base/jacket_male.webp, then scaled x1.0882 (shoulder seam to seam 17.00 -> 18.50 in, the width of a men's 40R service dress coat; neck seam to hem 28.68 -> 31.21 in, a 40R is about 31 in; CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.6 scaled by its 3 3/8 in nameplate gives a 25.20 x 31.99 in coat, the sheet is 25.27 x 32.09 in). Hardware is true size: buttons 7/8 in, nameplate 3 3/8 x 3/4 in, boards 4.55 in, letters. Silhouette traced from images/base/jacket_male.webp (581x719 px), true scale 0.05158 in/px, coat 32.13 in long, 25.27 in across the sleeves. Buttons (x 0.40, y 12.83/17.08/21.32 in), welt pocket (4.78 x 0.95 in at x 2.65, top y 11.07 in) and lower pocket flaps measured on CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.6 at the figure's own scale (its 3 3/8 in nameplate = 61.04 px/in); lapel, shirt and tie geometry traced.
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h}; polygons are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box
documented: single breasted, three buttons (Wing and Star or CAP Crest) (CAPR 39-1 4.1.5.2)
nameplate centred on wearer's right between sleeve seam and lapel, bottom even with the bottom of the ribbons (4.1.5.2.2.2)
lapel insignia halfway up the lapel seam (4.1.5.2.2.1)
officers wear gray epaulet sleeves, NCOs none (4.1.5.2): boards are the separate asset garment-blues-class-a-cadet-officer-insignia
assumed: scale: x1.0882 on the traced silhouette (shoulders 18.5 in and neck-seam-to-hem 31.2 in of a men's 40R, cross-checked on Fig 4.6 with the 3 3/8 in nameplate; the nameplate size itself is the Vanguard tag, not a regulation figure)
nameplate size (3.375 x 0.75 in = Vanguard CAP0599M cadet name plate (blue plastic, 3 3/8 x 3/4 in); no dimension in CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903; no dimension in CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903)
welt size (4.78 x 0.95 in measured on Fig 4.6; no regulation dimension)
lapel CAP letters approximated from the builder reference
